profile_text.body:
The material held here describes a Stanford research team, tracked under the product name Tutor CoPilot (Stanford research), which sits in the education and research AI space. The product is described as providing real-time suggestions to tutors. It is noted as not a commercial product, not for sale, and cited as a research model, with privacy marked as not applicable. The only link on file for it is a DOI reference to an arXiv paper.

The text harvested from the associated website is that of the DOI Foundation, not a Stanford research team. That site describes the DOI Foundation as a not-for-profit organization that governs the Digital Object Identifier system on behalf of agencies managing DOI registries, and as the registration authority for the ISO standard (ISO 26324) for the DOI system, governed by its Registration Agencies. It describes an international community of communities spanning areas including entertainment, standards, the built environment, natural history collections, scholarly communications, and research data, and explains that a DOI name is a persistent digital identifier for an object, usable by humans and machines, with a prefix starting with 10. and a suffix separated by a forward slash. The same page notes that Jonathan Clark, Managing Agent of the DOI Foundation since 2015, died on August 11, 2026.

No lawsuits, MCP servers, or SEC or patent facts are recorded for this entry.
